verification.notes: Confirmed through multiple sources. Brian Harpole, head of Charlie Kirk's security team, publicly shared text messages between Dan Flood (Turning Point USA security) and UVU Police Chief Jeff Long in interviews with Shawn Ryan and in news coverage. Multiple news outlets (Gateway Pundit, Salt Lake Tribune, Breitbart, Slay News) reported that Harpole presented these text messages showing the rooftop security communication. The texts showed warnings about student roof access at the Sorensen Center and Chief Long's response 'I got you covered.' The text exchange occurred on September 8, two days before the incident.

This is a big resignation as it pertains to September 10th, as it pertains to the Charlie Kirk assassination, as it pertains to the after action report, which we have now all read and adjusted and learned about. How effectively Turning Point USA and their affiliates were blaming wrongfully Jeff Long for a year of his life, a year of his life. They wanted the public to believe that the mistakes that were made were made because Police Chief Jeff Long did not do his job and they went so far as to and I would say this was it was cruel.

records.text: Brian Harpole criticized Jeff Long

appearances.snippet: We have some correspondence with the chief of the school on that day, on Monday before Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was killed and why this hadn't come out and why he won't stand up like a man and admit this, I don't know, but he's watching a bunch of men lose their careers and he's okay with it. ... On Monday before. ... This correspondence went to Chief Long (Jeff Long). Hello, Chief Long (Jeff Long). We received this message today from the student group.

records.text: Andrew Kolvet criticized Jeff Long

appearances.snippet: I think this is what a lot of people are keying in on the most. So TPUSA official, the security, texted, 'Hello, Chief Long (Jeff Long), we received this message today from the student group.' ... He said, quote, there is student roof access pretty close to where Charlie (Charlie Kirk) will be set up at Utah Valley and said it would be nice to either have it controlled access or allow one of my guys to be up there as well, if possible, Chief Long (Jeff Long). ... Texted, I got you covered, which obviously we know was not the case. They knew that that was a point of vulnerability. So if you know that that's a point of vulnerability that people can access that rooftop so easily, why was it left unguarded when you said you had the rooftops handled?

records.text: Text attribution disputed
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I can tell you right now, the reason why he describes his communication with the chief of the UVU police in an odd way is because it's not his communication. ... He's actually presenting a text message between Dan Flood and Chief Long.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens accused Brian Harpole of presenting a rooftop-security text exchange between Dan Flood and UVU Police Chief Jeff Long in a way that sounded like Harpole’s own communication.

records.text: Family notice reported
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So this morning I wake up and I see a trend on X that Charlie Kirk's family has filed a notice of claim against the state of Utah, also Utah Valley University Police Department, and more specifically UVU Police Chief Jeffrey Long and former president of UVU Astrid Tuminez, and others that are presently, quote unquote, presently under... ... The unknown who were involved in the death of Charlie Kirk. I don't know how they would be presently unknown, but OK, stick with me.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens reported that the Kirk family filed a notice of claim against Utah and named UVU officials over Charlie Kirk’s death.

records.text: Filing asserts broader coverage
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #15 (Ep aLJhpxrakCU)

appearances.snippet: They say this led TPUSA to reasonably conclude that UVU had a plan to address the identified risk and other similar risks, most obviously the risk from other rooftops, without TPUSA involvement. ... Chief Long (Jeffrey Long)'s text message did not invite or even allow Turning Point USA to take any steps to secure the risk of unsecured rooftops.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: As read on the show, the notice claims Long’s reply led TPUSA to expect UVU to address the identified and other rooftop risks without TPUSA involvement, and alleges it did not permit TPUSA to secure unsecured rooftops.

records.text: Walkway assurance scoped
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: We are told that Dan initiated that text exchange on September 8th, T minus two days regarding, again, the accessibility of that canopy area above the Hall of Flags. ... And that is when Jeff Long said, we got you covered in reference to, they make it clear, the Hall of Flags outdoor pedestrian walkway.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review identifies Flood’s September 8 exchange and Long’s assurance as concerning the Hall of Flags pedestrian walkway, adding report-based evidence to the dispute over broad rooftop framing.

records.text: UVU resource gaps retained
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: Chief Long (Jeff Long) did not initiate a mutual aid request to the Orem Police Department or other local public safety partners before the event, and additional external resources were not requested after the crowd size became apparent.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review also says Long did not request mutual aid before the event and external resources were not requested after the larger crowd became apparent.

records.text: EMP tip deemed unreliable
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: So they work with that government bureau when they are dealing with cybersecurity threats. Chief Long (Jeff Long) contacted S-I-A-C by email at approximately 7.30 a.m. on September 10th to share an anonymous tip to UVU. ... you received regarding a potential threat involving an electromagnetic pulse device that a suspect might be using at the event. ... Chief Long (Jeff Long) was seeking to determine whether any threat-related intelligence update was available regarding the tip. Long was advised email was the best method to request information from the Utah SIAC. ... The SIAC responded shortly thereafter to Chief Long (Jeff Long) that it was not a credible threat as it appeared the tipster had provided similar information in the past that was determined to be unreliable. I feel like this is an area that I would like to know more about.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review says Long sought SIAC intelligence about an anonymous EMP-device tip on the event morning and SIAC judged it not credible because the tipster had provided similar unreliable information.

records.text: Security contact date specified
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And yet UVU police chief Jeff Long is asking for a contact which he doesn't actually get. So on September 2nd, he follows up with them. He says, hey, still don't have a contact for the security. ... And so he reaches out to the club president. Again, this is per the independent review. And then he is supplied one. And on September 3rd, he is able to establish connection with Dan Flood. And I want to be clear, by the way, September 2nd is the first time that this upcoming event that we could find is mentioned.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Citing the independent review, Owens says Chief Long followed up for a security contact September 2 and established contact with Dan Flood September 3, specifying when the earlier coordination gap was bridged.

records.text: Long’s limited roof account
records.speaker: Jeff Long

appearances.snippet: And then Long (Jeff Long) said after I said that, he said. Well, Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s team should have gotten here early. ... I said, what does that have to do with it? He said, well, they got here the day of. They should have been here the day before. ... Again, what does that have to do with it? You said you had the roofs. And he said, well, it was just the roof above you. What do you mean the roof above you? Well, that bridge that was above you, that roof above, we had that because we didn't want people throwing stuff down on Charlie (Charlie Kirk).

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: In Turek’s reenactment of their later conversation, Long says Kirk’s team should have arrived the day before and police covered only the overhead roof or bridge to stop objects being thrown down.

records.text: Long resignation reported
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So I received a flurry of emails last night from people who work at UVU informing me that the rumor was, which I was able to confirm by getting in touch with these individuals, that Chief Jeff Long has resigned. ... I'm still looking for information as to whether he resigned willingly, whether he was forced out. I'm not sure. ... What I can tell you is that he has resigned and this is a... A big resignation. This is a big resignation as it pertains to September 10th, as it pertains to the Charlie Kirk assassination, as it pertains to the after action report, which we have now all read and adjusted and learned about.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens reports that UVU employee sources confirmed Jeff Long resigned and places the departure within her existing account of wrongful roof-security blame, while saying she does not know whether he left voluntarily or was forced out.

records.text: Possible legal escalation
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Legally, there is a term. acting in reckless disregard for the truth. I would say that Chief Jeff Long would definitely be able to meet that legal standard of demonstrating a reckless disregard for the truth because you have the people Who are employing Dan Flood, who have access to the messages, therefore have access to read through them to know exactly what they were speaking about, have access to the conversations, ... they could have spoken, they could have seen what he wrote back to them, what time he got there, they knew exactly what was being referred to in those text messages, and they pretended they didn't for over a year to the public, and Jeff Long was harassed for this.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens moves from alleging wrongful blame to arguing that Long could demonstrate reckless disregard for the truth and wondering whether he will sue TPUSA affiliates over the roof-message account.
